scenario_name: Benign lookalike (busy IT night, no attack)

lookalikes.detail: Interactive logon for kdurand via corporate VPN gateway, MFA satisfied
lookalikes.why_benign: Resembles external RDP access, but it is a known admin on the corporate VPN with MFA.
Resembles PowerShell payload execution, but it is the signed SCCM inventory task.

lookalikes.detail: Periodic HTTPS check-in to office365, ~2KB every 60s
lookalikes.why_benign: Resembles C2 beaconing, but the destination is Microsoft 365 and cadence is normal.

lookalikes.detail: MsMpEng.exe opened a handle to lsass.exe during scheduled AV scan
lookalikes.why_benign: Resembles LSASS credential access, but it is Microsoft Defender scanning.

lookalikes.detail: Network logon for svc_backup succeeded during nightly backup window
lookalikes.why_benign: Resembles a lateral-movement service logon, but it is the backup service account on schedule.

lookalikes.detail: Scheduled cloud backup upload, 512GB to Azure Blob Storage
lookalikes.why_benign: Resembles large-volume exfiltration, but it is the nightly backup to the known Azure tenant.
Resembles data collection, but apatel is in Finance and this is their own file.
Resembles HR data theft, but hokonkwo is in HR and routinely reads the roster.

lookalikes.detail: wevtutil.exe el (enumerate log names) by monitoring agent
lookalikes.why_benign: Resembles log tampering, but it only enumerates logs read-only; nothing is cleared.

lookalikes.detail: Kerberos TGT for administrator during the approved Tuesday patch window (MFA)
lookalikes.why_benign: Resembles credential abuse, but it is an admin during the scheduled patch window with MFA.

lookalikes.detail: git push over HTTPS 443, 40MB to corporate GitHub org
lookalikes.why_benign: Resembles outbound exfiltration, but it is a developer pushing code to GitHub.

lookalikes.detail: cmd.exe /c whoami (run during a helpdesk troubleshooting call)
lookalikes.why_benign: Resembles host discovery, but it is a single benign command during a support call.

lookalikes.detail: SMB session to FILESRV-02:445 for scheduled web asset sync
lookalikes.why_benign: Resembles lateral movement, but it is a documented app-to-fileserver content sync.

lookalikes.detail: Network logon for rgarcia succeeded (Finance share access)
lookalikes.why_benign: Resembles unauthorized access, but rgarcia is in Finance and uses this share daily.
Resembles data staging, but it is the scheduled backup job writing to the backup volume.
Resembles a malicious rundll32 proxy, but it is the normal Windows shell handler.

note: There is no attack. Each lookalike event resembles a technique but is individually benign, and they share no pivot host, credential, or external destination. A correct analysis draws no attack chain (or only dashed, unverified fragments), never a connected intrusion.
